facility_roles.quote: PandaX-III (Particle And Astrophysical Xenon Experiment III) will search for the NLDBD of 136Xe at the China Jin Ping underground Laboratory (CJPL).

intervals.label: first TPC module under construction
intervals.note: Start is the date of the design paper (arXiv v1, 27 October 2016), which says the first module is under construction. A November 2023 status paper says 'The construction of the detector was completed. The detector will be installed at the CJPL-II after the performance test in Shanghai.' No later source was found on installation; the PandaX website (checked 2026-10-26) calls PandaX-III 'a R&D effort to develop a high pressure gaseous Xenon TPC'. The status 'construction' is therefore the last documented stage, not a statement about 2026.
intervals.quote: The first 200 kg module is under construction and is expected to be deployed in the next 2-3 years.

quantity.note: The 2016 design paper gave 200 kg for the first module; the 2020 TPC paper and the 2023 status paper give about 140 kg.
quantity.quote: It can hold about 140 kg of xenon (90% enriched) at an operating pressure of 10 bar.

name: PandaX-III
notes: Belongs to the PandaX programme (PandaX-I, II, 4T and xT); the collaboration record is the existing collaboration:pandax-4t ('PandaX Collaboration').

Meets the inclusion bar through a design report that names its site (arXiv:1610.08883, CJPL) and a 2023 status paper reporting the final detector constructed. No physics result exists. The official PandaX page describes PandaX-III as 'a R&D effort'; the integrator may prefer status `proposed`.

physics_goals.quote: The PandaX-III experiment searches the neutrinoless double beta decay of 136 Xe with a high-pressure xenon gaseous time projection chamber (TPC).
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double beta decay of 136Xe with a high-pressure gaseous xenon time projection chamber read out by Micromegas

summary.plain: A planned high-pressure xenon-gas detector for the Jinping underground laboratory in China, meant to look for neutrinoless double beta decay of xenon-136 by recording the tracks of the two electrons. The detector has been built and tested above ground; installation underground was still pending in 2023.
summary.technical: PandaX-III: cylindrical high-pressure gas TPC (120 cm x 160 cm active volume) with about 140 kg of 90 % enriched 136Xe at 10 bar, charge readout by 52 thermal-bonding Micromegas modules (20 x 20 cm2), to sit in a water-tank or dry shield at CJPL-II (2400 m of rock); topological discrimination expected to give 0.49 background counts per year in the region of interest.
